title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook (Comprehensive)
author: Ava Patel
content:
Overview
--------
This playbook describes Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response process. It combines the incident lifecycle, runbooks for common failure modes, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations and handoffs, game day guidance, and status page / customer communications templates. The document is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and product leads who participate in incidents or own service reliability.

Goals
- Restore customer-facing functionality as quickly and safely as possible.
- Preserve data integrity and minimize cost of remediation.
- Communicate clearly internally and externally.
- Capture learnings and action items via timely postmortems.

Scope
Covers hosted Redwood API, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployment support processes. For infra-specific procedures (cloud accounts, on-prem packaging), see related runbooks in eng-infra and eng-private-deployments.

Incident Severity & SLOs
-----------------------
We use four severity levels. Severity assignment is conservative; escalate if uncertain.

1) Sev 1 (P0) — Major customer impact, production outage
- Symptom: API unavailable for many customers, control plane unreachable, or severe data loss risk.
- Business impact: Significant revenue or SLA hit.
- Target: Acknowledge in 5 minutes, mitigation plan within 30 minutes.

2) Sev 2 (P1) — Severe degradation
- Symptom: High latency (p95 above threshold), large volume of 5xx errors, or major feature broken for many customers.
- Target: Acknowledge in 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 60 minutes.

3) Sev 3 (P2) — Partial degradation
- Symptom: Single-region impact, single feature degraded, or small subset of customers affected.
- Target: Acknowledge in 2 hours, resolution within 48 hours.

4) Sev 4 (P3) — Minor / informational
- Symptom: Cosmetic issue, non-critical telemetry anomaly, or backlog of small bugs.
- Target: Acknowledge in 3 business days.

Service-level objectives (examples)
- Redwood API (hosted): Availability >= 99.95% per region per month.
- Inference latency SLO (small requests): p95 < 400ms; for large generations SLO depends on model class and should be documented per model in the model catalog.
- Control plane: Availability >= 99.9%

Incident Lifecycle (high level)
------------------------------
1. Detection & Alerting
   - Alerts originate from Prometheus/Datadog, SLO burn alerts, on-call PagerDuty, or customer reports (support, status page).
   - On-call engineer acknowledges the PagerDuty alert immediately per severity targets.

2. Triage
   - Determine scope (services, regions, customers) and severity.
   - Assign incident lead (usually the on-call SRE/owner) and note primary comms channel (#incidents/<id> Slack).

3. Respond & Mitigate
   - Follow relevant runbook. Prioritize containment over root cause.
   - If mitigation requires rolling back, perform with a safe rollback checklist.

4. Escalation
   - If the on-call cannot mitigate within the target time, escalate to the next guardrail (service owner, team lead, engineering manager, CTO on-call as needed).

5. Post-incident
   - When service is restored, send a status update and capture a postmortem within 72 hours (severe incidents must have an initial draft within 48 hours).
   - Track action items and verify closures.

Runbooks (common incidents)
--------------------------
Each runbook contains: detection signals, immediate mitigation steps, containment commands, rollback steps, verification, and post-incident checks. Below are examples; full runbooks live under eng-infra and eng-serving-runtime.

A) Hosted API high 5xx rate / spike in errors
Detection:
- Alerts: >0.5% 5xx rate sustained for 5m or >SLO error budget burn.
- Dashboards: API gateway 5xx, model-server 5xx, queue lengths.

Immediate mitigation:
1. Confirm scope: curl health endpoints for public and internal API.
2. If traffic surge suspected, enable rate limiting or emergency global throttling:
   - CLI: rdctl rate-limit set --scope=global --limit=200rps (example)
3. Warp traffic to fallback model (if model-serving errors): update routing policy to fallback variant with compatible interface.

Containment & rollback:
- If a recent deploy correlates, rollback the deploy using the release pipeline: ci-cd rollback --service api-gateway --to-tag <last-stable>.
- If cache corruption suspected, invalidate prefix cache: redis-cli --scan-match "kvcache:*" | xargs redis-cli del

Verification:
- Confirm error rates drop below threshold for 15m and p95 latency stabilizes.

B) Model-serving OOM / GPU failures
Detection:
- GPU OOM alerts, increased model-worker restarts, degraded throughput.

Immediate steps:
1. Pause new model deployments and autoscaling.
2. Drain affected node: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
3. If recurrence, switch traffic to compatible quantized or smaller variant (see model-catalog for exact variant ids).

Mitigation:
- Reduce batch size and max_seq_length in the routing config:
  api update-routing --model <id> --max-batch 4 --max-seq 512

C) Database connectivity / write errors
Detection:
- Increased errors writing to metadata DB, retry storms, connection pool saturation.

Mitigation:
1. Engage DB runbook: check replicas, failover status, and connection pools.
2. Throttle background sync jobs and pause non-critical writes.
3. If master is unhealthy, perform controlled failover per DB provider steps (see eng-infra/db-failover-runbook).

On-call Rotations & Handoffs
---------------------------
Roles
- Primary on-call: first responder and incident lead for runtime incidents during their shift.
- Secondary on-call: backup for overflow and escalation; supports primary for longer incidents.
- Pager duty escalation policy: primary -> secondary (5m unanswered) -> on-call manager -> eng-sre lead -> EM -> CTO on-call (rare).

Rotation cadence
- Primary rotation: 1 week. Secondary rotation: 2 weeks. Night/weekend schedules split across APAC/US on-call to maintain regional coverage.

Handoff checklist (on every shift change)
1. Confirm calendar and PagerDuty schedule are correct.
2. Review open incidents and action item list.
3. Check pending follow-ups from previous handoff.
4. Verify SLA/SLO dashboards are green or known-degraded.
5. Document any ongoing mitigations in the #incidents channel.

Escalation policy (quick summary)
- If mitigation is not in progress within the severity target, escalate to the team lead.
- If mitigation requires cross-team coordination (infra, network, security), page the on-call for those teams and open a cross-team bridge.

Game Days
---------
Purpose
- Validate runbooks, practice cross-team communication, and measure mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for critical failure modes.

Cadence & ownership
- Quarterly for high-severity scenarios; monthly for targeted critical services. Owned by eng-sre with rotating engineering partners.

Example scenarios
- Region failover: simulate entire us-west region loss and fail traffic to us-east.
- Model regression: deploy a canary model that intentionally returns a 500 for a specific request shape and exercise rollback playbooks.

Game day metrics to capture
- Time to detection, time to acknowledge, time to mitigation, time to restore, communication lag, and postmortem completion time.

Postmortems & Action Items
-------------------------
Postmortem requirements
- All Sev 1/2 incidents must have a postmortem. Sev 3 incidents should have a postmortem if they produced customer impact or recurring issues.
- Initial draft due within 48 hours for Sev 1/2; final postmortem with action items and owners within 7 days.

Postmortem template (required sections)
1. Title and incident id
2. Summary (brief customer-facing description)
3. Timeline (UTC timestamps)
4. Impact (customers, regions, revenue/SLA exposure)
5. Root cause analysis (what exactly failed)
6. Mitigations (what was done during incident)
7. Long-term fixes and action items (owner + due date)
8. Follow-ups and verification plan
9. Lessons learned

Action item tracking
- Create tasks in the engineering project board and tag leads; link tasks in the postmortem. Close verification tasks only after validation steps complete and confirm in follow-up comment.

Status Page & Customer Communications
----------------------------------
Status channels
- Public status page: status.redwood.ai (update cadence: initial within 30 minutes of Sev1, updates every 60 minutes until resolved; Sev2 within 60 minutes, then every 2-4 hours).
- Customer comms: Support creates targeted messages for affected customers where SLA credits or degraded performance is expected.

Templates (use as starting point)
- Initial public status message (Sev1 example):
  Title: Major service disruption — Redwood API (us-west)
  Status: Investigating
  Impact: Customers in us-west may experience failed requests and higher latency.
  Started: 2026-02-10T14:12Z
  Next update: 2026-02-10T14:42Z
  Notes: Our on-call team is investigating.

- Internal Slack update (first post):
  [INC-2026-123] Sev1 — API outage in us-west. PagerDuty acknowledged. Primary on-call: @ava.patel. Bridge: <zoom-link>. Initial hypothesis: TLS termination errors on gateway after deploy. Action: rolling back last deploy (tag: release-2026-02-10). ETA 30m.

- Customer targeted email (for affected enterprise accounts):
  Subject: Service disruption affecting Redwood API in us-west — ongoing
  Body: We are aware of an issue affecting API request success rates in the us-west region. Our engineers are investigating and we will provide updates every hour. We apologize for the impact and will follow up with a post-incident report.

- Resolved public status message:
  Title: Service restored — Redwood API (us-west)
  Status: Resolved
  Impact: Service returned to normal for all affected customers.
  Resolved: 2026-02-10T15:03Z
  Postmortem: Link will be published in 72 hours.

Ownership & Contacts
-------------------
- On-call roster lives in PagerDuty (link internal).
- Engineering leadership escalation contacts: Miguel Santos (eng-sre lead), Priya Iyer (VP Eng), Ben Carter (CTO on-call).
- Support escalation: Customer Success PagerDuty for high-touch customers.

Monitoring & Dashboards
---------------------
Key dashboards (owner in parentheses)
- API Health (eng-platform) — p50/p95/p99 latency, 4xx/5xx rates, request volume.
- Model-serving health (eng-serving-runtime) — GPU utilization, OOMs, worker restarts, batch sizes.
- SLO burn and error budget (eng-sre) — projected burn rate, alerts for accelerated burn.

Alert tuning guidance
- Avoid noisy alerts: require 2/3 rule (alert fires only if >2 of 3 key signals exceed thresholds for 5 minutes).
- Use deduplication keys in alerting to avoid alert storms for identical root cause.

Post-incident verification
------------------------
- For each action item, the owner must provide verification evidence: dashboards, smoke tests, or test request logs.
- Close postmortem only after all critical action items have verification and a date for follow-up.

Appendices
---------
A. Quick CLI snippets
- Restart model-worker group (Kubernetes): kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/model-worker-<model-id>
- Check API gateway health: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq .
- Invalidate Redis prefix: REDIS_CLI="redis-cli -h redis.internal"; $REDIS_CLI keys "kvcache:*" | xargs $REDIS_CLI del

B. Postmortem checklist
- Draft created (Y/N)
- Timeline included (Y/N)
- Owners assigned for action items (Y/N)
- Postmortem published and link added to status page (Y/N)

C. Glossary
- MTTM: Mean Time To Mitigate
- SLO: Service Level Objective
- OOM: Out Of Memory

Related pages
- eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture
- eng-infra/db-failover-runbook

Document maintenance
- Owner: eng-sre.
- Review cadence: Quarterly or after any Sev1 incident.
- How to propose updates: Open PR against this page with suggested changes and include at least one reviewer from eng-sre.
